sentences.text: Yeneen is a titanosaur sauropod dinosaur, with its type species designated as Yeneen houssayi.
The genus name honors an entity from the Tehuelche culture linked to cold weather, while the species name commemorates Nobel laureate Bernardo Alberto Houssay for supporting CONICET.
Leonardo S. Filippi and colleagues formally described this dinosaur in 2026.
The genus contains only one known species, based on a partial skeleton found at the La Invernada site within the Bajo de la Carpa Formation in Argentina, designated as the holotype.
Three specimens reside in the Museo Municipal Argentino Urquiza: the holotype, a single right ilium from a smaller individual, and a third set of disarticulated bones currently under preparation.
Phylogenetic analysis places Yeneen in the clade Saltasauroidea, specifically in a subgroup called "Clade A" where it diverges after Narambuenatitan and before Overosaurus.
This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago in the Santonian age of Argentina.
